name: EntryVault for Contact Form 7
author: Saqib K.

sections.description:
EntryVault for Contact Form 7 is an independent third-party plugin that stores every successful Contact Form 7 submission in custom database tables, gives you a searchable and filterable admin dashboard, lets you view individual entries, and exports to CSV or JSON in one click.

This plugin is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Contact Form 7 project or its author.

Key Features

  • Automatic capture – hooks into wpcf7_mail_sent; zero configuration needed.
  • Custom DB tables – scalable two-table design (wp_cf7_entries + wp_cf7_entry_meta).
  • Admin dashboard – WP_List_Table-based entries list with sortable columns, search, form filter, date-range filter, and pagination.
  • Single entry view – clean detail page showing every submitted field.
  • Bulk & single delete – with nonce-protected confirmation.
  • CSV export – UTF-8 BOM included for Excel compatibility; respects current filters; protected against spreadsheet formula injection; streamed, so large exports do not run out of memory.
  • JSON export – machine-readable; respects current filters.
  • CSV import – import CSV files exported from the Contact Form CFDB7 plugin or from EntryVault itself, with duplicate detection and a row-by-row report.
  • REST API – GET /evcf7/v1/entries, GET/DELETE /evcf7/v1/entries/{id}, GET /evcf7/v1/analytics (admin-only; also available under cf7em/v1).
  • Analytics page – per-form submission counts with progress bars.
  • Settings page – control whether data is preserved or deleted on plugin removal.
  • Developer hooks – do_action('evcf7_after_entry_saved', ...) and apply_filters('evcf7_entry_data', ...).
  • Performance – indexed DB columns; assets loaded only on plugin pages; batch meta queries.
  • Security – nonces on all forms and actions; all inputs sanitised; all outputs escaped; fully prepared SQL queries.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0 or later
  • PHP 7.4 or later
  • Contact Form 7 (any recent version)

Developer Hooks

Action – fired after an entry is saved:

do_action( 'evcf7_after_entry_saved', $entry_id, $form_id, $fields, $contact_form );

Filter – modify field data before it is stored:

add_filter( 'evcf7_entry_data', function( $fields, $form_id, $contact_form ) {
    unset( $fields['your-hidden-field'] );
    return $fields;
}, 10, 3 );

Action – fired after a CSV row is imported:

do_action( 'evcf7_after_cfdb7_import', $entry_id, $cfdb7_id, $fields );

Filter – turn off the CSV formula protection (default on):

add_filter( 'evcf7_csv_escape_formulas', '__return_false' );

REST API

All endpoints require manage_options capability (administrator). The same routes are available under two namespaces, evcf7/v1 and cf7em/v1.

GET    /wp-json/evcf7/v1/entries
GET    /wp-json/evcf7/v1/entries/{id}
DELETE /wp-json/evcf7/v1/entries/{id}
GET    /wp-json/evcf7/v1/analytics

Supported query parameters for the list endpoint: form_id, status (read|unread), date_from, date_to (YYYY-MM-DD, compared with the stored UTC date), search, per_page (max 100), page, orderby (id|form_id|status|created_at), order (ASC|DESC). The total count is returned in the X-EVCF7-Total and X-EVCF7-TotalPages headers. Dates in responses are UTC.

The analytics endpoint returns form_id, form_title, total and unread for each form.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the entryvault-contact-form-7 folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through Plugins → Installed Plugins.
  3. A new EntryVault CF7 menu appears in the WordPress admin sidebar.
  4. Ensure Contact Form 7 is installed and active.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin modify Contact Form 7 in any way?

No. It only listens to the wpcf7_mail_sent action hook, which CF7 fires after a form is submitted successfully. No CF7 files are touched.

Is this plugin officially affiliated with Contact Form 7?

No. EntryVault for Contact Form 7 is an independent third-party plugin. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or in any way connected with the Contact Form 7 project or its author.

Will existing submissions be imported automatically?

Not automatically. You can import a previously exported CFDB7 CSV via EntryVault CF7 → Import CSV.

Can I export only a subset of entries?

Yes. Apply your filters (date range, search keyword, read/unread) on the entries page before clicking Export CSV or Export JSON.

Which time zone are dates in?

The admin screens show dates in your site’s time zone (Settings → General), and the date filter uses your time zone too. Dates are stored in UTC, and CSV, JSON and REST API output give the stored UTC value. Entries imported from a CFDB7 file before version 1.4.3 are shown exactly as they were in the file.

Why do some values in the CSV start with an apostrophe?

Values that begin with =, +, - or @ could run as formulas when the file is opened in Excel or Google Sheets, which is a known security risk. EntryVault adds an apostrophe in front of them. When you import the file back into EntryVault, the apostrophe is removed again.

Where is the data stored?

In two custom database tables: {prefix}cf7_entries and {prefix}cf7_entry_meta. No data is sent to any external server.

Does uninstalling the plugin delete my data?

No, not by default. When you delete the plugin, your stored entries and database tables are preserved so reinstalling later restores all data. To delete everything on uninstall, go to EntryVault CF7 → Settings and enable the data-deletion option.

Is it compatible with CFDB7?

Yes. CSV exports use the same column format as CFDB7 (Id, Date, Status, Name, Email, Subject, Message) so data can be freely moved between both plugins. When importing, choose whether the file comes from CFDB7 (dates in site time) or from EntryVault (dates in UTC).

I was using “CF7 Entries Manager & Export” — do I need to migrate?

No. Version 1.3.0 is a direct rename/rebrand of “CF7 Entries Manager & Export”. Your existing database tables, settings, and entries are fully preserved. Simply update the plugin; no migration is required.
sections.changelog:
1.4.4 (November 26, 2026)

  • Fixed: The plugin’s stylesheet and script now load on every EntryVault screen (Entries, entry view, Analytics, Import CSV, Settings). Since the rename in 1.3.0 they loaded on the main screen only, so for example the bars on the Analytics page were invisible.
  • Fixed: The “(No form)” row on the main, Analytics and Import screens now opens only the entries that belong to no form (link fid=none), instead of every entry. CSV and JSON export from that list contain the same entries.
  • Fixed: Bulk “Delete” on the entries list now asks for confirmation first.
  • Fixed: Line breaks in long fields (such as the message) were shown twice on the entry view, leaving large gaps.
  • Changed: Only EntryVault’s own short confirmations (“entries deleted”, “Settings saved”) hide themselves after 5 seconds; import results and other plugins’ notices stay until closed.

1.4.3 (November 26, 2026)

  • Fixed: The REST API is now available under both evcf7/v1 and cf7em/v1. Earlier versions documented cf7em/v1 but only served evcf7/v1.
  • Fixed: Dates on the admin screens are shown in the site time zone, and the date filter (and the export of a filtered list) uses site-local days. Stored dates are unchanged; CSV, JSON and REST still give UTC.
  • Fixed: CFDB7 imports convert the file’s site-time dates to UTC. New “File Source” choice on the Import screen for re-importing EntryVault’s own CSV files (dates in UTC, duplicates matched by Id and date).
  • Fixed: Unrecognised dates in an imported file are reported row by row (the row is still imported with the current date, as before).
  • Fixed: CSV and JSON exports are streamed in batches, so large exports no longer run out of memory. The files are the same as before.
  • Security: CSV export protects against spreadsheet formula injection; the importer removes the protection again so values round-trip exactly.
  • Fixed: Single entry view no longer shows other plugins’ notices twice, and Delete asks for confirmation only once.
  • Fixed: The read/unread filter is kept when you search or filter by date, and the active filter is shown next to the heading.
  • Fixed: Forms with both your-name and name (or similar) no longer get two columns with the same header in the CSV.
  • Fixed: The “Entries per page” screen option now works.
  • Fixed: Searching no longer matches every entry for words such as “mail”.
  • Fixed: “(No form)” is shown for entries imported without a form; non-Latin form titles show the correct initial.
  • Improved: Imports check duplicates once per batch of 200 rows and save each entry’s fields in one query.
  • Improved: The plugin now runs its database check after an update, not only on activation (no database changes in this release).
  • REST API: new optional status and orderby parameters on the entries list; unread count added to analytics; date parameters are validated.
  • Removed unused stylesheet rules and duplicate inline CSS; the screens look the same.
  • Added a translation template (languages/entryvault-contact-form-7.pot).

1.4.2

  • Fixed: Entries are now saved even when email delivery fails (wpcf7_mail_failed hook added), matching CFDB7 behaviour — no submission is ever lost.
  • Improved: Single-entry sidebar now shows Mail Status (Delivered / Failed) and a warning banner for failed-mail entries.
  • Updated: Contributor list updated; Author field corrected.

1.4.1

  • Fixed: Updated “Tested up to” to WordPress 7.1 to resolve outdated_tested_upto_header error on WordPress.org.
  • Improved: Forms landing page now uses full-width layout with WordPress native table styling, no custom CSS.
  • Improved: Entries list toolbar rebuilt using WP native search_box(), tablenav, alignleft/alignright — zero custom styling required.

1.4.0

  • Fixed: Single-entry detail card now uses inline style attributes instead of relying solely on enqueued/inline stylesheets, guaranteeing correct rendering in all hosting environments (including WordPress Playground) regardless of how the CSS pipeline behaves.
  • Added: Requires Plugins: contact-form-7 header so WordPress checks Contact Form 7 is installed/active before allowing activation.
  • Fixed: Removed raw <style> tag; styles now output exclusively via wp_enqueue_style() / wp_add_inline_style() and inline style attributes, per WordPress.org Plugin Check requirements.

1.3.0

  • Rebranded: Plugin renamed from “CF7 Entries Manager & Export” to “EntryVault for Contact Form 7”.
  • Updated: Text Domain changed to entryvault-contact-form-7 to match WordPress.org slug.
  • Updated: Admin menu labels and page titles updated to new branding.
  • Compatibility: All existing database tables, option names, hook names, and REST API endpoints are fully preserved — no migration required for existing users.

1.2.0

  • Fixed: Text Domain header updated to match WordPress.org plugin slug, resolving textdomain_mismatch error.

1.1.2

  • Fixed: Select-all checkbox fully self-contained JavaScript implementation.
  • Fixed: Correct <thead>/<tfoot> wrapping in list table for proper DOM structure.

1.1.1

  • Fixed: Asset enqueue page hooks corrected (evcf7-forms_page_* pattern).
  • Improved: Filter toolbar, bulk-actions bar, and item-count row spacing.

1.1.0

  • Added: CFDB7-compatible CSV import with duplicate detection.
  • Added: Status column (read/unread) mirroring CFDB7.
  • Added: Settings page with data-on-uninstall control.
  • Fixed: Search and date filters use GET form so filters appear in URL.
  • Fixed: Admin notices captured above entry detail card.
  • Improved: All SQL queries use $wpdb->prepare() for full WPCS compliance.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
